close_reason: Applied the sealed-trait pattern to 7 extension-client traits that lacked it: JmapMailExt (canonical), JmapCalendarsExt, JmapTasksExt, JmapContactsExt, JmapFileNodeExt, JmapSharingExt, JmapMetadataExt. jmap-chat-client::JmapChatExt was already sealed pre-existing (via mod sealed::Sealed) — adopted that exact pattern verbatim for consistency: a private mod sealed { pub trait Sealed {} impl Sealed for ::jmap_base_client::JmapClient {} } block plus a 'pub trait JmapXExt: sealed::Sealed' constraint on the trait declaration. Each trait's rustdoc now carries the canonical 'This trait is **sealed**: implementations outside this crate are not permitted.' note explaining that sealing keeps adding methods to the trait a non-breaking change. Workspace canonical-template propagation rule followed: changed mail-client first, then propagated cookie-cutter to the 6 remaining unsealed siblings in the same pass. Cheap-now-expensive-later fix landed pre-publish per the bead's recommendation; no third-party impls exist outside the workspace today so no caller-side breakage.
title: JmapMailExt trait is unsealed — third-party impls forbid future trait expansion
